parent: AmplifyBio, LLC (venture-backed Battelle spinout; Battelle Memorial Institute reabsorbed it in 2025)
notes: Contract research and manufacturing firm launched by Columbus-based Battelle in 2021 with sites in West Jefferson and New Albany; JobsOhio's September 2024 executed-grants report lists 155 jobs retained and 263 committed on a $132.75 million investment, and NBC4 reported more than 200 employees laid off when the company shut down in April 2025. Its own closure notice calls it a startup dependent on investors, so it was not a Battelle subsidiary at the grant date; Battelle took it back in an October 2025 assignment for the benefit of creditors.

The payee is the US holding company of Louis Dreyfus Company, the Dutch-French agricultural trader founded in 1851, which says on its own site that it employs over 20,000 people in more than 100 countries. The project entity in JobsOhio's December 2024 report is Louis Dreyfus Company Upper Sandusky LLC, a $541 million soybean crushing plant in Wyandot County with 114 jobs committed, so the money built the company's own plant.

Columbus ordinance 2574-2025, granting this LLC a ten-year enterprise zone abatement, names the contact as David Pizzotti, principal and co-founder of Trident Capital Group, 15 E. Broad St. Suite 200, Boston MA, matching the payee's Boston address. The grant is a JobsOhio Spec Development (OSIP) award with jobs listed as TBD for a speculative industrial park in east Columbus that Trident is building to lease, so the payee is a developer's project vehicle, not an operating company. No headcount is published for Trident, a small private real-estate firm, so the bucket is inferred.

ELO stands for East Liverpool, Ohio: this is the project entity through which True North, LLC, a West Virginia high-tech business services firm (accounting, payroll, medical billing, collections) with 55 employees, renovated the 31,000 square foot BOSS Building as its own new corporate headquarters. JobsOhio's release names the company, its 55 existing employees and 25 planned additions, so the payee is an operating company building its own building, not a developer.

parent: The James B. Oswald Company (Oswald Companies)
notes: Employee-owned Cleveland insurance brokerage; the JobsOhio release on its downtown Cleveland headquarters move lists 320 jobs retained and 88 committed, and JobsOhio's March 2024 report records a $500,000 Revitalization Grant on a $6 million investment. The grant paid for the company's own headquarters fit-out, so it is classed as a business.

parent: Modula S.p.A. (Immobiltec USA Inc is the group's US property-owning affiliate)
notes: Franklin, Ohio's major site plan file for the $24 million Modula expansion at 5000 Commerce Center Drive lists IMMOBILTEC USA, INC. as the owner of that parcel, and the stated purpose is to consolidate Modula's own warehouse and distribution operations into its plant. Modula S.p.A., the Italian maker of automated vertical storage systems, is headquartered in Casalgrande (Reggio Emilia) and says it has three production sites, 14 subsidiaries and over 1,000 employees. Immobiltec is the group's real-estate arm, so the operating company behind the payee is Modula; the exact Immobiltec-to-Modula ownership chain is not published, which is why this is graded C.

Advanced-manufacturing R&D company at 130 E South Street, Barnesville, Ohio, which describes itself on its own site as a small business rooted in eastern Ohio. JobsOhio's October 2024 report shows a $350,000 Revitalization Grant in Belmont County with 3 jobs retained and 15 committed on a $1.0 million investment, so the money went to its own facility. Independent; no parent found.

parent: Brennan Holdings, LLC (joint venture with Ray Fogg Corporate Properties, LLC)
notes: Ray Fogg Corporate Properties states that it partnered with 'BH (Ohio) Leasing, LLC (an affiliate of Brennan Holdings, LLC)' to develop Seasons Business Park at Route 8 and Seasons Road in Stow, starting with a speculative 108,000 square foot industrial building. JobsOhio's June 2021 report records a Spec Development (OSIP) grant with zero jobs created or retained on a $15.7 million investment, so this is a developer's project vehicle building to lease. Brennan Holdings is the Akron real-estate company of David Brennan; the Longmont, Colorado address on the 990 is a manager's address and the earlier FY2022 filing gave an Akron address, so the Ohio HQ is the better read but is graded C.
